items.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: You see, Jim, just like you always say about Jim. Jim, he's my friend.

ctx.x: Look, don't be afraid what you're going to say. We can save these tapes and not play them for anybody. I say this is for a hundred years from now. You know, if you want to, we can put like a restriction on it, they call it, you know, and not to be played for ten years, you know, or something. So don't worry, just speak your mind.
Sure. You know what I mean? That's all you can do, you don't think you need to know. You see, Jim, just like you always say about Jim. Jim, he's my friend.
Yeah, we all know that. We know your buddies, yeah.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while.

ctx.x: Let's see, I thought Sonny played with Chris for a while.

Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while. Yeah, Sonny played with Chris for a while. Good while, too. Sonny went with, with, uh, at the Lick with, lived with, uh, Emmis White. Went to Lick, the half-road house, they call it. Wrecked with Emmis White. What kind of house? Eh?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: But Sonny could tell you all them fellas' names, because he used to play in that band with him,

ctx.x: Who were some of the people in the bands down there?

Oh, well, I'll tell you, a lot of them people is dead. I couldn't remember all them people's names. I just thought you could tell us- But Sonny could tell you all them fellas' names, because he used to play in that band with him,
you know? I thought maybe some of them were here, you could tell us where to find them, you know?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: Him and Sonny Henry, Sonny on trombone, Peer on bass. Amos White on trumpet.

ctx.x: He's living out in California today.
Yeah, I see, I, I met Amos in San Francisco. Mm hmm. Yeah, Peer, where the, where the chance is is a long time. Mm hmm. Him and Sonny Henry, Sonny on trombone, Peer on bass. Amos White on trumpet.

I thought of a guy with that bass from down there. Hmm? I thought of somebody with that bass that played with dance bands here. Mm hmm. There's a guy that played string bass from down there. Uh, from, uh, Dear Reigns came up here. Uh, uh. Little Jim?
